original_question: Which gene responsible for causing Arthrogryposis–renal dysfunction–cholestasis syndrome belongs to the Sec1 domain family?

final_qi.question: Which gene responsible for causing Arthrogryposis–renal dysfunction–cholestasis syndrome belongs to the Sec1 domain family?
final_qi.search_keyword: Arthrogryposis renal dysfunction cholestasis syndrome Sec1 domain family gene
final_qi.long_answer: The gene responsible for causing Arthrogryposis–renal dysfunction–cholestasis syndrome that belongs to the Sec1 domain family is VPS33B. This gene encodes the human homolog of a protein involved in vesicle trafficking, and its mutations have been found to cause ARC syndrome. Studies indicate that VPS33B is a member of the Sec1 domain family, which plays a critical role in regulating SNARE-dependent membrane fusion within the endosome/lysosome pathway.

Section: Introduction
Vacuolar protein sorting-associated protein 33B is a protein that in humans is encoded by the VPS33B gene.[5][6]
Section: Function
Vesicle mediated protein sorting plays an important role in segregation of intracellular molecules into distinct organelles. Genetic studies in yeast have identified more than 40 vacuolar protein sorting (VPS) genes involved in vesicle transport to vacuoles. This gene is a member of the Sec-1 domain family, and encodes the human ortholog of rat Vps33b which is homologous to the yeast class C Vps33 protein. The mammalian class C Vps proteins are predominantly associated with late endosomes/lysosomes, and like their yeast counterparts, may mediate vesicle trafficking steps in the endosome/lysosome pathway.[6]
